claims.evidence: This is cited knowledge about H2A.Z eviction.

claims.claim: Within an AA, AZ or ZZ nucleosome, the two L1 loop regions of the histone fold domains of the opposing H2A and/or H2A.Z molecules come into contact with each other at an interface that passes through the nucleosomal dyad.
claims.source: Within an AA, AZ or ZZ nucleosome, the two L1 loop regions of the histone fold domains of the opposing H2A and/or H2A.Z molecules come into contact with each other at an interface that passes through the nucleosomal dyad, but not when the histones are outside of the nucleosomal structure (Luger et al., 1997; Suto et al., 2000) (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: This is structural knowledge cited from the literature and shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: The L1 loop regions of H2A and/or H2A.Z do not come into contact when the histones are outside of the nucleosomal structure.
claims.source: Within an AA, AZ or ZZ nucleosome, the two L1 loop regions of the histone fold domains of the opposing H2A and/or H2A.Z molecules come into contact with each other at an interface that passes through the nucleosomal dyad, but not when the histones are outside of the nucleosomal structure (Luger et al., 1997; Suto et al., 2000) (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: This is structural knowledge cited from the literature and shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: The L1-L1' interface is ideal for the placement of cysteine probes for in vivo disulfide crosslinking.
claims.source: Thus, the L1-L1' (prime represents the symmetrical nucleosomal counterpart) interface is ideal for the placement of cysteine probes for in vivo disulfide crosslinking.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural knowledge about the L1-L1' interface.

claims.claim: Only when histones are inserted into nucleosomes will the cysteine pairs be close enough to form disulfide bonds.
claims.source: The assumption is that only when histones are inserted into nucleosomes will the cysteine pairs be close enough to form disulfide bonds, allowing crosslinking efficiency to act as a metric for the global occupancy of H2A and H2A.Z (these histones naturally lack cysteine).
claims.evidence: This is a stated assumption underlying the VivosX approach.

claims.claim: H2A and H2A.Z naturally lack cysteine.
claims.source: The assumption is that only when histones are inserted into nucleosomes will the cysteine pairs be close enough to form disulfide bonds, allowing crosslinking efficiency to act as a metric for the global occupancy of H2A and H2A.Z (these histones naturally lack cysteine).
claims.evidence: This is stated knowledge about the amino acid composition of H2A and H2A.Z.

claims.claim: All six HTZ1(Cys)FL alleles fully complemented the formamide sensitivity of the htz1∆ mutant.
claims.source: All six HTZ1(Cys)FL alleles fully complemented the formamide sensitivity of the htz1∆ mutant (Figure 1C) (Wu et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is a functional complementation result shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: Wild-type core histones of yeast do not contain any cysteine.
claims.source: Since wild-type core histones of yeast do not contain any cysteine, the Htz1(Cys)FL protein contributes the only sulfhydryl group to the nucleosome.
claims.evidence: This is stated knowledge about yeast histone composition.

claims.claim: The Htz1(Cys)FL protein contributes the only sulfhydryl group to the nucleosome.
claims.source: Since wild-type core histones of yeast do not contain any cysteine, the Htz1(Cys)FL protein contributes the only sulfhydryl group to the nucleosome.
claims.evidence: This is a logical inference from the fact that wild-type yeast histones lack cysteine.

claims.claim: In the presence of 4-DPS, the H2A.Z-to-H2A.Z crosslinking adducts (ZxZ), which migrate at ~37 kD, were detected for cysteines substituted at A45, T46, G47 and R48, but not H44 or T49.
claims.source: In the presence of 4-DPS, the H2A.Z-to-H2A.Z crosslinking adducts (ZxZ), which migrate at ~37 kD, were detected for cysteines substituted at A45, T46, G47 and R48, but not H44 or T49 (Figure 1D–E, top panels).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1D-E.

claims.claim: The disulfide crosslinking efficiency does not correlate particularly well with Cα-Cα' proximity.
claims.source: The disulfide crosslinking efficiency, which is defined as the ratio of ZxZ over total H2A.Z immunoblotting signals, does not correlate particularly well with Cα-Cα' proximity, suggesting that the L1-L1' interface is dynamic (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The L1-L1' interface is dynamic.
claims.source: The disulfide crosslinking efficiency, which is defined as the ratio of ZxZ over total H2A.Z immunoblotting signals, does not correlate particularly well with Cα-Cα' proximity, suggesting that the L1-L1' interface is dynamic (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lack of correlation between crosslinking efficiency and Cα-Cα' distance.

claims.claim: The formation of the ZxZ adduct for A45C, T46C, G47C, and R48C was accompanied by a reduction in the FLAG-tagged Htz1(Cys)FL monomer (mono Z) at ~17 kD.
claims.source: The formation of the ZxZ adduct for A45C, T46C, G47C, and R48C was accompanied by a reduction in the FLAG-tagged Htz1(Cys)FL monomer (mono Z) at ~17 kD (Figure 1D–F).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claims.claim: Under reducing SDS-PAGE conditions where β-mercaptoethanol (β-ME) was added to the gel loading buffer, all ZxZ adducts were cleaved and the Htz1(Cys)FL mutant proteins migrated as monomers.
claims.source: Under reducing SDS-PAGE conditions where β-mercaptoethanol (β-ME) was added to the gel loading buffer, all ZxZ adducts were cleaved and the Htz1(Cys)FL mutant proteins migrated as monomers (Figure 1D–E, bottom panels).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1D-E demonstrating that the adducts are disulfide-bonded.

claims.claim: The HTZ1(T46C)FL mutant was chosen for subsequent VivosX experiments because it also efficiently crosslinked to an L1' cysteine mutant in H2A.
claims.source: The HTZ1(T46C)FL mutant was chosen for subsequent VivosX experiments because it also efficiently crosslinked to an L1' cysteine mutant in H2A (see below).
claims.evidence: This is a stated rationale for the choice of mutant for further experiments.

claims.claim: The effectiveness of the NEM blocking step was confirmed by the inhibition of total protein labeling with the thiol-specific fluorescence reagent, Alexa647-maleimide.
claims.source: The effectiveness of the NEM blocking step was confirmed by the inhibition of total protein labeling with the thiol-specific fluorescence reagent, Alexa647-maleimide (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, compare Lanes 1 and 3) and by the inhibition of formation of non-specific disulfide crosslinking adducts of Htz1(T46C)FL (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B, compare Lanes 1 and 3).
claims.evidence: This is experimental validation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claims.claim: The effectiveness of the NEM blocking step was confirmed by the inhibition of formation of non-specific disulfide crosslinking adducts of Htz1(T46C)FL.
claims.source: The effectiveness of the NEM blocking step was confirmed by the inhibition of total protein labeling with the thiol-specific fluorescence reagent, Alexa647-maleimide (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, compare Lanes 1 and 3) and by the inhibition of formation of non-specific disulfide crosslinking adducts of Htz1(T46C)FL (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B, compare Lanes 1 and 3).
claims.evidence: This is experimental validation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claims.claim: The duration for the extraction of precipitated histones by the TUNES buffer was empirically determined to be 60 min as it allows maximal solubilization of the histones without any appreciable reduction of the disulfide adducts.
claims.source: The duration for the extraction of precipitated histones by the TUNES buffer was empirically determined to be 60 min as it allows maximal solubilization of the histones without any appreciable reduction of the disulfide adducts (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C–D).
claims.evidence: This is an optimization result shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C-D.

claims.claim: All immunoblots were conducted using a pan-H2A antibody (Active Motif) since this antibody gave a stronger signal than the V5 antibody.
claims.source: Although the mutated HTA1(Cys) alleles contain an N-terminal fusion to the V5 epitope, all immunoblots below were conducted using a pan-H2A antibody (Active Motif) since this antibody gave a stronger signal than the V5 antibody (not shown).
claims.evidence: This is a stated methodological choice based on antibody performance.

claims.claim: All five V5HTA1(Cys) mutants rescued the inviability caused by loss of the URA3 plasmid, indicating that H2A function was not impaired by the cysteine substitutions.
claims.source: This inviability was rescued by each one of the V5HTA1(Cys) mutants carried on the HIS3 plasmid, indicating that H2A function was not impaired by the cysteine substitutions (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This is functional complementation data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: AxA crosslink adducts were observed for the H2A N39C, Y40C, A41C, and Q42C mutant proteins, but not G38C.
claims.source: Using the VivosX method described above but probing with anti-H2A antibodies, AxA crosslink adducts were observed for the H2A N39C, Y40C, A41C, and Q42C mutant proteins, but not G38C (Figure 2C–D).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2C-D.

claims.claim: The lack of G38C crosslinking can be explained by a long Cα-Cα' distance (13.2 Å).
claims.source: While the lack of G38C crosslinking can be explained by a long Cα-Cα' distance (13.2 Å), the crosslinking efficiency of the other four H2A L1 loop sites does not correlate well with Cα-Cα' proximity (Figure 2E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) (White et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on structural information cited from White et al., 2001.

claims.claim: The crosslinking efficiency of the other four H2A L1 loop sites does not correlate well with Cα-Cα' proximity.
claims.source: While the lack of G38C crosslinking can be explained by a long Cα-Cα' distance (13.2 Å), the crosslinking efficiency of the other four H2A L1 loop sites does not correlate well with Cα-Cα' proximity (Figure 2E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) (White et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claims.claim: A41C and Q42C exhibited robust crosslinking despite having a Cα-Cα' distance of >10 Å.
claims.source: In fact, A41C and Q42C exhibited robust crosslinking despite having a Cα-Cα' distance of >10 Å.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the data highlighting the lack of correlation between distance and crosslinking efficiency.

claims.claim: An increase in AxA adducts was accompanied by a reciprocal decrease in monomeric H2A (mono A) in a 4-DPS-dependent manner.
claims.source: Similar to Htz1(Cys)FL, an increase in AxA adducts was accompanied by a reciprocal decrease in monomeric H2A (mono A) in a 4-DPS-dependent manner (Figure 2C–D, top panels and Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2C-D and Figure 2E.

claims.claim: The AxA species was lost when the proteins were exposed to β-ME, further confirming that AxA is caused by disulfide crosslinking at the cysteine sites.
claims.source: The AxA species was lost when the proteins were exposed to β-ME, further confirming that AxA is caused by disulfide crosslinking at the cysteine sites (Figure 2C–D, bottom panel).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2C-D demonstrating that the adducts are disulfide-bonded.

claims.claim: Low levels of AxA crosslinks were detected for N39C, Y40C, A41C and Q42C even in the absence of 4-DPS.
claims.source: Note that low levels of AxA crosslinks were detected for N39C, Y40C, A41C and Q42C even in the absence of 4-DPS. This may reflect the natural redox state of the nucleus (Dardalhon et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the data with a speculative interpretation.

claims.claim: Low levels of AxA crosslinks in the absence of 4-DPS may reflect the natural redox state of the nucleus.
claims.source: Note that low levels of AxA crosslinks were detected for N39C, Y40C, A41C and Q42C even in the absence of 4-DPS. This may reflect the natural redox state of the nucleus (Dardalhon et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the background crosslinking observed.

claims.claim: For the V5HTA1(N39C) HTZ1(T46C)FL double mutant, two crosslinked species were observed when the blots were probed with either anti-FLAG or anti-H2A to detect H2A.Z and H2A, respectively.
claims.source: For the V5HTA1(N39C) HTZ1(T46C)FL double mutant, two crosslinked species were observed when the blots were probed with either anti-FLAG or anti-H2A to detect H2A.Z and H2A, respectively (Figure 3A, lane 6 and Figure 3B, lane 6).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claims.claim: For H2A.Z, the top band exhibited the same mobility as ZxZ.
claims.source: In each case, one band of the doublet co-migrated with the homotypic adduct. For H2A.Z, the top band exhibited the same mobility as ZxZ (Figure 3A, lanes 6 and 8), while the lower band of the H2A doublet co-migrated with AxA.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: The lower band of the H2A doublet co-migrated with AxA.
claims.source: In each case, one band of the doublet co-migrated with the homotypic adduct. For H2A.Z, the top band exhibited the same mobility as ZxZ (Figure 3A, lanes 6 and 8), while the lower band of the H2A doublet co-migrated with AxA.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: The differences in ZxZ and AxA mobility are consistent with the observation that monomeric Htz1(T46C)FL migrates slower than monomeric V5Hta1(N39C) despite the fact that the calculated molecular weight of Htz1(T46C)FL is actually smaller (16.6 kD versus 16.8 kD), possibly due to the strong negative charge of the FLAG epitope.
claims.source: The differences in ZxZ and AxA mobility are consistent with the observation that monomeric Htz1(T46C)FL migrates slower than monomeric V5Hta1(N39C) despite the fact that the calculated molecular weight of Htz1(T46C)FL is actually smaller (16.6 kD versus 16.8 kD), possibly due to the strong negative charge of the FLAG epitope (Figure 3A–B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the data with a speculative explanation.

claims.claim: A doublet was observed only when V5HTA1(N39C) and HTZ1(T46C)FL were combined, suggesting that one band of the doublet represents V5Hta1(N39C) crosslinked to Htz1(T46C)FL (AxZ).
claims.source: A doublet was observed only when V5HTA1(N39C) and HTZ1(T46C)FL were combined, suggesting that one band of the doublet represents V5Hta1(N39C) crosslinked to Htz1(T46C)FL (AxZ) (Figure 3A–B, lane 6).
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the data shown in Figure 3A-B.

claims.claim: Realignment of the two halves of the blot demonstrated that the predicted AxZ band contains both V5Hta1 and Htz1FL and runs between the ZxZ and AxA adducts.
claims.source: Realignment of the two halves of the blot demonstrated that the predicted AxZ band contains both V5Hta1 and Htz1FL and runs between the ZxZ and AxA adducts (Figure 3C, top panel).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3C confirming the identity of the AxZ band.

claims.claim: All the crosslinked proteins were eliminated when fractionated on a gel in the presence of β-ME, confirming that, similar to ZxZ and AxA, the AxZ adduct was also generated by disulfide crosslinking.
claims.source: All the crosslinked proteins were eliminated when fractionated on a gel in the presence of β-ME, confirming that, similar to ZxZ and AxA, the AxZ adduct was also generated by disulfide crosslinking (Figure 3C, bottom panel).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3C demonstrating that the AxZ adduct is disulfide-bonded.

claims.claim: The assumption is that only histones in close proximity in assembled nucleosomes will crosslink and therefore the AxA, AxZ, and ZxZ signals derived from whole cell extracts accurately reflect the native AA, AZ and ZZ nucleosomal levels.
claims.source: An advantage of VivosX is that it uses whole cell extracts, thereby obviating the need to purify chromatin, which greatly facilitates high-throughput experiments. The assumption is that only histones in close proximity in assembled nucleosomes will crosslink and therefore the AxA, AxZ, and ZxZ signals derived from whole cell extracts accurately reflect the native AA, AZ and ZZ nucleosomal levels.
claims.evidence: This is a stated assumption underlying the VivosX approach.

claims.claim: Similar ratios of the various crosslinked species should be observed when native nucleosomes are extracted from cells before they are used for crosslinking.
claims.source: If true, then similar ratios of the various crosslinked species should be observed when native nucleosomes are extracted from cells before they are used for crosslinking.
claims.evidence: This is a prediction based on the assumption that whole cell extracts accurately reflect nucleosomal levels.

claims.claim: The ratios of AxZ to ZxZ (1:0.2) or AxZ to AxA (1:3.5) in native nucleosomes were similar to those observed with the V5HTA1(N39C) HTZ1(T46C)FL double mutant using total extracts (1:0.3 and 1:4.2, respectively).
claims.source: The ratios of AxZ to ZxZ (1:0.2) or AxZ to AxA (1:3.5) in native nucleosomes (Figure 3D, lanes 3 and 5) were similar to those observed with the V5HTA1(N39C) HTZ1(T46C)FL double mutant using total extracts (1:0.3 and 1:4.2, respectively) (Figure 3A–C, averaged values).
claims.evidence: This is a comparison of data from Figure 3D with Figure 3A-C validating the whole cell extract approach.

claims.claim: Higher levels of the AxA, AxZ, and ZxZ adducts were present in native nucleosomes than whole cell extracts of the untreated cells.
claims.source: Higher levels of the AxA, AxZ, and ZxZ adducts were present in native nucleosomes than whole cell extracts of the untreated cells (Figure 3D, 4-DPS minus lanes).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: The higher background oxidation in native nucleosomes was likely due to atmospheric oxidation of the dithiols during the cell lysis, chromatin preparation and/or MNase digestion steps.
claims.source: This difference was likely due to atmospheric oxidation of the dithiols during the cell lysis, chromatin preparation and/or MNase digestion steps.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the higher background in native nucleosomes.

claims.claim: Such background oxidation was minimized in the whole cell extracts as cells were fixed by TCA and extraction was performed in the presence of the thiol blocker NEM.
claims.source: Such background oxidation was minimized in the whole cell extracts as cells were fixed by TCA and extraction was performed in the presence of the thiol blocker NEM.
claims.evidence: This is an explanation for why whole cell extracts have lower background oxidation.

claims.claim: In the absence of SWC5, H2A.Z levels at promoters are decreased.
claims.source: SWC5 encodes a component of the SWR complex that is required for its H2A.Z deposition activity at promoters (Tramantano et al., 2016). In the absence of SWC5, H2A.Z levels at promoters are decreased (Tramantano et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is cited knowledge about the effect of SWC5 deletion.

claims.claim: ZxZ adducts were observed in the extracts from the SWC5 strain, but not swc5∆.
claims.source: ZxZ adducts were observed in the extracts from the SWC5 strain, but not swc5∆ (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Mutants swc5(1-232) and swc5(LDW→3A) significantly reduced ZxZ crosslinking efficiency in VivosX.
claims.source: Additional mutants of SWC5 that were previously shown to prevent H2A.Z deposition include a truncation of the highly conserved BCNT domain [swc5(1-232)] and substitution of the LDW motif within BCNT with alanines [swc5(LDW→3A)] (Sun and Luk, 2017) (Figure 4A). These mutants also significantly reduced ZxZ crosslinking efficiency in VivosX (Figure 4B–C).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4B-C.

claims.claim: swc5∆ HTZ1(T46C)FL carrying SWC5 on a plasmid has a lower ZxZ crosslinking efficiency than HTZ1(T46C)FL with endogenous SWC5.
claims.source: Note that swc5∆ HTZ1(T46C)FL carrying SWC5 on a plasmid has a lower ZxZ crosslinking efficiency than HTZ1(T46C)FL with endogenous SWC5 (compare Figure 4 to Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: This is an observation comparing data from Figure 4 to Figure 1F.

claims.claim: The discrepancy in ZxZ crosslinking efficiency could be due to loss of the SWC5 plasmid in a fraction of cells during growth of the culture.
claims.source: The discrepancy could be due to loss of the SWC5 plasmid in a fraction of cells during growth of the culture.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed difference.

claims.claim: ZZ nucleosomes are normally removed from the +1 position at promoters by formation of the transcriptional preinitiation complex (PIC).
claims.source: ZZ nucleosomes are normally removed from the +1 position at promoters by formation of the transcriptional preinitiation complex (PIC) (Tramantano et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is cited knowledge about ZZ nucleosome eviction.

claims.claim: ZZ nucleosomes accumulate when their disassembly is inhibited by depletion of the TATA-binding protein (TBP), which is required for PIC recruitment.
claims.source: As a result, ZZ nucleosomes accumulate when their disassembly is inhibited by depletion of the TATA-binding protein (TBP), which is required for PIC recruitment (Hahn, 2004).
claims.evidence: This is a logical inference from the cited knowledge about TBP's role in PIC recruitment.

claims.claim: A reproducible increase of ZxZ adducts and a concomitant decrease of mono Z was observed after TBP-FRB depletion.
claims.source: A reproducible increase of ZxZ adducts and a concomitant decrease of mono Z was observed after TBP-FRB depletion (N = 3), consistent with our earlier quantitative ChIP-seq results (Figure 5A, compare lanes 6 and 8) (Tramantano et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5A consistent with prior ChIP-seq results.

claims.claim: ZxZ crosslinks were reduced when SWC5-FRB was depleted by Anchor-away.
claims.source: By contrast, ZxZ crosslinks were reduced when SWC5-FRB was depleted by Anchor-away (N = 3) (Figure 5A, lanes 10 and 12).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: VivosX can accurately report the global chromatin dynamics of H2A.Z.
claims.source: VivosX can therefore accurately report the global chromatin dynamics of H2A.Z.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments showing VivosX correctly reports changes in H2A.Z occupancy.

claims.claim: Blocking PIC assembly by depleting TBP-FRB preferentially increased the ZxZ adduct, indicating that ZZ nucleosomes, but not AZ nucleosomes, were targeted by PIC for removal.
claims.source: Blocking PIC assembly by depleting TBP-FRB preferentially increased the ZxZ adduct, indicating that ZZ nucleosomes, but not AZ nucleosomes, were targeted by PIC for removal (Figure 5B–C).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding from the data shown in Figure 5B-C.

claims.claim: Monomeric H2A.Z is diminished reciprocally when ZZ nucleosomes accumulate, consistent with the free pool of Z-B dimers being used by SWR to generate more ZZ nucleosomes, but without being replenished by PIC-dependent ZZ nucleosome disassembly.
claims.source: In fact, monomeric H2A.Z is diminished reciprocally, consistent with the free pool of Z-B dimers being used by SWR to generate more ZZ nucleosomes, but without being replenished by PIC-dependent ZZ nucleosome disassembly (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the data with reference to the model in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The increase in the ZxZ adduct and the corresponding decrease in monomeric H2A.Z were small but reproducible in three biological replicates and statistically significant, with non-overlapping standard deviations and p values of < 0.05 based on t-tests.
claims.source: While the increase in the ZxZ adduct and the corresponding decrease in monomeric H2A.Z were small, these differences were reproducible in three biological replicates and statistically significant, with non-overlapping standard deviations and p values of < 0.05 based on t-tests.
claims.evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the data demonstrating significance.

claims.claim: Human H2A.Z has two isoforms (H2A.Z.1 and H2A.Z.2), and they are encoded by the H2AFZ and H2AFV genes, respectively.
claims.source: Human H2A.Z has two isoforms (H2A.Z.1 and H2A.Z.2), and they are encoded by the H2AFZ and H2AFV genes, respectively (Vardabasso et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is cited knowledge about human H2A.Z isoforms.

claims.claim: H2A.Z(H43C) corresponds to the yeast Htz1(R48C), which has a similar crosslinking efficiency as the Htz1(T46C) used in most yeast experiments.
claims.source: H2A.Z(H43C) corresponds to the yeast Htz1(R48C), which has a similar crosslinking efficiency as the Htz1(T46C) used in most yeast experiments (Figure 1B and F).
claims.evidence: This is a comparison based on data shown in Figure 1B and F.

claims.claim: H2A.Z(H43C) was chosen for human VivosX, instead of H2A.Z(T41C), because the crosslinking efficiency of Htz1(R48C) was slightly better than Htz1(T46C) in preliminary experiments.
claims.source: H2A.Z(H43C) was chosen for human VivosX, instead of H2A.Z(T41C) [cognate amino acid of yeast (T46C)] because the crosslinking efficiency of Htz1(R48C) was slightly better than Htz1(T46C) in our preliminary experiments (data not shown).
claims.evidence: This is a stated rationale for the choice of mutant for human experiments.

claims.claim: The H2A.Z(H43C)V5 protein exhibited a more complex pattern of crosslinked proteins than yeast Htz1(T46C)FL.
claims.source: The H2A.Z(H43C)V5 protein exhibited a more complex pattern of crosslinked proteins than yeast Htz1(T46C)FL (Figure 6A, lane 4).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Four slower migrating bands appeared above the expected monomeric H2A.Z(H43C)V5.
claims.source: Four slower migrating bands appeared above the expected monomeric H2A.Z(H43C)V5.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the data in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: The top three bands in H2A.Z(H43C)V5 lane were disulfide adducts that occur at the H43C position because these bands were not observed in the cells expressing wild-type H2A.ZV5.
claims.source: The top three bands in H2A.Z(H43C)V5 lane were disulfide adducts that occur at the H43C position because these bands were not observed in the cells expressing wild-type H2A.ZV5 (Figure 6A, compare lanes 2 and 4).
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the comparison of data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: When the same lysate of H2A.Z(H43C)V5 was treated with β-ME, the top three bands disappeared.
claims.source: In addition, when the same lysate of H2A.Z(H43C)V5 was treated with β-ME, these three bands disappeared (compare Lane four in Figure 6A–B).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 6A-B demonstrating that the bands are disulfide-bonded.

claims.claim: The H2A.Z band near the 25 kD marker could represent a ubiquitylated form of H2A.Z.
claims.source: Since the H2A.Z band near the 25 kD marker is not due to crosslinking, it could represent a ubiquitylated form of H2A.Z, as suggested by Sarcinella et al. (2007).
claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on cited literature.

claims.claim: Mutation of two ubiquitylation sites at K120 and K121 to arginines in the H2AFZV5 and H2AFZ(H43C)V5 alleles reduced the amount of the ~25 kD band in the absence of 4-DPS, indicating that this band represents monoubiquitylated H2A.Z.
claims.source: To test this idea, two (of three) ubiquitylation sites at K120 and K121 were mutated to arginines in the H2AFZV5 and H2AFZ(H43C)V5 alleles. Both mutants reduced the amount of the ~25 kD band in the absence of 4-DPS, indicating that this band represents monoubiquitylated H2A.Z (Figure 6A, lanes 5–8).
claims.evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 6A confirming the identity of the ubiquitylated band.

claims.claim: The two slowest crosslinked adducts were almost eliminated in the H2AFZ(H43C,KK→RR)V5 mutant, with a corresponding increase in the remaining adduct, suggesting that the ~30 kD band is the ZxZ disulfide adduct of two non-ubiquitylated H2A.Z monomers.

results.result: VivosX is a novel in vivo disulfide crosslinking method that uses strategically positioned cysteine pairs on interacting proteins to capture site-specific protein-protein interactions within cells. The method exploits the reducing environment of the nucleus and cytosol, which prevents spontaneous disulfide formation, but allows crosslinking under oxidizing conditions induced by membrane-permeable oxidants like 4-DPS.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C12-14, C28-29, C38-40 collectively establish the conceptual and mechanistic foundation of VivosX. The method is well-defined, relies on established knowledge about cellular redox environments (C13, C27, C28), and uses structural information to guide cysteine placement (C12, C29, C38). The assumption that only nucleosome-incorporated histones crosslink (C39) is central to the method and is validated by subsequent experiments.

results.result: VivosX successfully detects H2A.Z-to-H2A.Z (ZxZ) crosslinks in yeast using cysteine substitutions at the L1 loop region. Four of six tested positions (A45C, T46C, G47C, R48C) showed 4-DPS-dependent ZxZ adducts that were reversible under reducing conditions. Crosslinking efficiency did not correlate well with Cα-Cα' distance, suggesting the L1-L1' interface is dynamic.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-49 describe the initial validation of VivosX in yeast H2A.Z. The functional complementation (C41), detection of specific crosslinked species (C44), reversibility with β-ME (C48), and lack of correlation with structural distances (C45-46) provide strong experimental support. The inference about interface dynamics (C46) is reasonable given the data, though speculative. Controls and replicates appear adequate (Figure 1).

results.result: The VivosX protocol includes critical quality control steps: NEM effectively blocks free thiols post-lysis to prevent artifactual crosslinking, and the 60-minute TUNES extraction time optimally solubilizes histones while preserving disulfide bonds.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-52 describe methodological validations shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3. The NEM blocking is confirmed by two independent assays (Alexa647-maleimide labeling and prevention of non-specific crosslinks), and the extraction time is empirically optimized. These controls strengthen confidence in the method's specificity.

results.result: VivosX detects H2A-to-H2A (AxA) crosslinks in yeast using cysteine substitutions in the H2A L1 loop. Four of five positions (N39C, Y40C, A41C, Q42C) showed 4-DPS-dependent AxA adducts that were β-ME-reversible. Similar to H2A.Z, crosslinking efficiency did not correlate with Cα-Cα' distance, with some positions showing robust crosslinking despite >10 Å distances.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-60 demonstrate VivosX works for H2A-H2A interactions. Functional complementation (C54), specific crosslink detection (C55), reversibility (C60), and the lack of distance correlation (C56-58) parallel the H2A.Z results. The observation of background crosslinking without 4-DPS (C61-62) is noted but does not undermine the main findings. Data in Figure 2 support these claims.

results.result: VivosX detects heterotypic H2A-to-H2A.Z (AxZ) crosslinks in yeast double mutants expressing both V5HTA1(N39C) and HTZ1(T46C)FL. The AxZ band migrates between ZxZ and AxA adducts, contains both H2A and H2A.Z as confirmed by dual antibody detection, and is reversible with β-ME.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-69 describe the detection of heterotypic nucleosomes, a key capability of VivosX. The experimental design using split membranes probed with different antibodies (C68, Figure 3C) provides strong evidence for the AxZ identity. The β-ME reversibility (C69) confirms disulfide bonding. This demonstrates VivosX can distinguish all three nucleosome configurations (AA, AZ, ZZ).

results.result: Crosslinked species detected in whole cell extracts accurately reflect native nucleosome composition. The ratios of AxZ:ZxZ and AxZ:AxA in whole cell extracts (1:0.3 and 1:4.2) closely match those in purified native nucleosomes (1:0.2 and 1:3.5), validating the use of whole cell extracts for VivosX.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-75 address a critical assumption of VivosX (C70). The comparison between whole cell extracts and native nucleosomes (C72, Figure 3D) provides strong validation. The explanation for higher background in native nucleosomes (C73-75) is reasonable. This result supports the practical utility of VivosX without chromatin purification.

results.result: VivosX correctly reports decreased global H2A.Z occupancy in mutants defective for H2A.Z deposition. Deletion of SWC5 or mutations in its BCNT domain (swc5(1-232), swc5(LDW→3A)) significantly reduced ZxZ crosslinking efficiency, consistent with their known roles in H2A.Z deposition.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-78 demonstrate VivosX can detect biologically relevant changes in H2A.Z occupancy. The results are consistent with prior knowledge about SWC5 function (C76) and show appropriate controls. The observation about plasmid-borne SWC5 (C79-80) is noted but does not undermine the main conclusion. Data in Figure 4 support these claims with replicates.

results.result: VivosX correctly reports increased global H2A.Z occupancy when H2A.Z eviction is blocked. Depletion of TBP-FRB by Anchor-away increased ZxZ crosslinks and decreased monomeric H2A.Z (N=3, p<0.05), while depletion of SWC5-FRB decreased ZxZ crosslinks, demonstrating VivosX accurately reports global H2A.Z chromatin dynamics.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-85 provide critical validation of VivosX by showing it detects both increases and decreases in H2A.Z occupancy. The use of Anchor-away for conditional depletion is appropriate, results are consistent with prior ChIP-seq data (C83), statistical analysis is provided (C88), and biological replicates are included. Figure 5A data support these claims.

results.result: VivosX reveals that the transcription machinery preferentially disassembles ZZ nucleosomes over AZ nucleosomes. Blocking PIC assembly by TBP-FRB depletion preferentially increased ZxZ adducts while decreasing monomeric H2A.Z, with changes that were small but reproducible across three biological replicates and statistically significant (p<0.05).
results.evaluation: Claims C6-7, C86-88 describe a novel biological finding enabled by VivosX's ability to distinguish ZZ from AZ nucleosomes. The experimental design is sound (1 hr depletion before crosslinking, C109), statistical analysis is provided (C88), and the interpretation is logical given the data (Figure 5B-C). This demonstrates VivosX can address questions not easily answered by other methods.

results.result: VivosX works in human MCF10A cells. Expression of H2A.Z(H43C)V5 in human cells produced 4-DPS-dependent crosslinked species that were absent in wild-type H2A.Z and were eliminated by β-ME treatment, demonstrating VivosX is applicable across species.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C89-95 demonstrate VivosX extends to human cells. The choice of H43C position is justified (C90-91), appropriate controls are included (wild-type H2A.Z), and β-ME reversibility confirms disulfide bonding (C95). The more complex pattern in human cells (C92-93) is explained by ubiquitination (see next result). Figure 6 data support these claims.

results.result: VivosX distinguishes ZZ nucleosomes with different ubiquitination states in human cells. The method detected non-ubiquitinated ZxZ, mono-ubiquitinated ZxZ (uZxZ), and di-ubiquitinated ZxZ (uZxuZ) species. Mutation of ubiquitination sites (K120/K121→RR) confirmed band identities, and the two ubiquitin moieties are on opposite faces of the ZZ nucleosome.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C96-103 describe a sophisticated application of VivosX to detect post-translational modification stoichiometry. The experimental design using K120/K121→RR mutants (C97-98, C100) provides strong evidence for band assignments. The deduction about ubiquitin placement (C102) is logical and consistent with prior literature (C103). This demonstrates VivosX's utility beyond simple interaction detection. Figure 6 data support these claims.

results.result: Ectopic H2A.Z expression in human cells is ~5-fold higher than endogenous levels, which may cause misincorporation and affect the observed distribution of modified and unmodified H2A.Z.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-105 acknowledge an important caveat of the human cell experiments. The overexpression is documented (Figure 6—figure supplement 2) and the potential for artifacts is appropriately noted (C105). This limitation does not invalidate the demonstration that VivosX works in human cells, but does limit interpretation of the biological significance of the ubiquitination patterns observed.

results.result: The authors acknowledge potential 'observer effect' artifacts where crosslinking might perturb chromatin dynamics. To mitigate this, H2A.Z deposition/eviction was blocked for ≥1 hr before crosslinking in validation experiments, though indirect interference cannot be ruled out.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-110 discuss an important limitation. The experimental design consideration (C109) is appropriate, but the authors acknowledge they cannot rule out indirect effects (C110). The fact that VivosX correctly reported known changes in H2A.Z occupancy (C5, C85) provides some reassurance, but the concern remains valid. This is appropriately presented as a caveat rather than a fatal flaw.

results.result: 4-DPS treatment does not dramatically affect bulk Z-to-Z crosslinking through oxidative stress responses. Similar ZxZ levels were observed with or without sodium azide (which blocks ATP-dependent processes), though genomic rearrangement of ZZ nucleosomes cannot be ruled out.
results.evaluation: Claims C111-113 address oxidative stress concerns with a control experiment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D-E). The azide experiment (C112) provides some reassurance about bulk effects, but the caveat about genomic rearrangement (C113) is appropriately noted. This control is useful but not definitive, as azide may not fully block all stress responses.

results.result: The L1-L1' interface is dynamic, as evidenced by robust crosslinking at positions with Cα-Cα' distances >7 Å and at solvent-inaccessible positions. Multiple factors including conformational dynamics, solvent accessibility, and local biochemical environment affect crosslinking efficiency, explaining the lack of correlation with static structural distances.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-46, C57-58, C114-123 provide a mechanistic interpretation of the crosslinking data. The observation of crosslinking at unexpected positions (C115, C116) is well-documented. The proposed explanations involving conformational dynamics (C117-118, C120) and biochemical factors (C121-123) are reasonable and supported by cited literature (C119, C121). The 'clamshell' model (C119-120) is speculative but plausible.

results.result: The majority of nucleosomes in the double mutant are expected to crosslink upon 4-DPS treatment, with uncrosslinked species representing non-nucleosomal H2A-H2B and H2A.Z-H2B dimer pools (39% and 26% of total, respectively). These may be associated with chaperones, remodelers, or exist as hexasomes or non-nucleosomal complexes.
results.evaluation: Claims C124-128 interpret the uncrosslinked species in the data. The expectation of efficient crosslinking (C125) is supported by cited in vitro work (C124). The quantification of uncrosslinked pools (C126) is data-based (Figure 3). The speculations about dimer associations (C127-128) are reasonable and appropriately presented as possibilities with citations.

results.result: Endogenous cysteines outside ~15 Å from the intended probe should not interfere with VivosX, as demonstrated by lack of crosslinking at distant positions (H44C, T49C, G38C). Endogenous cysteines near interaction interfaces could potentially be exploited as probes.
results.evaluation: Claims C129-130 provide practical guidance for applying VivosX to other proteins. The argument is supported by negative controls (C129) showing no crosslinking at distant positions. The suggestion about exploiting endogenous cysteines (C130) is reasonable speculation for future applications.

results.result: No 4-DPS-dependent H3 C110-C110' crosslinking was detected in human cells despite efficient H2A.Z L1-L1' crosslinking, consistent with prior findings that H3 C110 is inaccessible to thiol-specific reagents without nucleosome destabilization.
results.evaluation: Claims C131-133 describe a negative result that validates VivosX specificity. The lack of H3 crosslinking (C132, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) despite efficient H2A.Z crosslinking demonstrates the method's selectivity. The consistency with prior literature (C133) strengthens this interpretation.

results.result: The L1-L1' interface of ZZ nucleosomes in human cells is solvent accessible and dynamic, as evidenced by efficient crosslinking at H43C despite an 8.2 Å Cα-Cα' distance. Crosslinking of monoubiquitylated H2A.Z suggests this accessibility is independent of transcription.
results.evaluation: Claims C134-136 extend the dynamics findings to human cells. The efficient crosslinking despite large distance (C134-135) parallels yeast findings. The observation about ubiquitylated H2A.Z in heterochromatin (C136) provides additional support for transcription-independent dynamics, though this inference is somewhat speculative.

results.result: VivosX is a versatile method applicable to diverse protein-protein interactions beyond histones, including transcription factor dimers (bHLH-LZ), post-translational modification stoichiometry (PCNA), and potentially cytosolic interactions. The method is simple, cost-effective, and applicable from yeast to humans.
results.evaluation: Claims C10, C137-152 discuss future applications and overall conclusions. While VivosX is demonstrated for histones in yeast and human cells (C150-152, SUPPORTED), the suggested applications to other systems (C137-146) are speculative. The claim about cytosolic applicability (C147-149) is based on cited work with GFP but not directly demonstrated. These are reasonable extrapolations but require experimental validation.
